For the Appellant(s) : Mr. H. Gupta, Central Government Counsel (through Video  Conferencing).
For the Respondent(s) : Mr. A.R. Malhotra, Advocate assisted by Mr. Jonathan L. Sailo,
Advocate for respondent Nos.1 to 53.
: Mr. Samuel Vanlalhriata Chhangte, Additional Advocate General, Mizoram for respondent Nos.54 to 57.
Page No.# 8/14 - BEFORE - HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. ASHUTOSH KUMAR HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MICHAEL ZOTHANKHUMA 06.11.2025 (Ashutosh Kumar, CJ) We have heard Mr. H. Gupta, learned Central Government Counsel for the appellants/State and Mr. A.R. Malhotra and Mr. Jonathan L. Sailo,
learned Advocates for the respondent Nos.1 to 53.

The N.F. Railways, for construction of Railway Lines had acquired a large tracts of lands located in Kolasib District for construction of Railway Line from Bairabi to Sairang, by way of Award No.1 of 2012.
This had displaced approximately 592 land owners whose names found mention in the Award No.1 of 2012.
They were granted compensation for crops but the compensation for land was granted only to two of the land owners who were found to be holding Land Settlement Certificates.
The remaining 590 of the land owners had only Village Council Passes and Annual Periodic Pattas, which were not taken into consideration as evidence good enough for holding them as land owners.
The possession of all the land was taken on 13.03.2013.
The respondent Nos.1 to 53 fell in the same category of 590 persons who had been only paid for the crops and structures built on the land, and not for the land.

sentences.text: Out of those 590 owners of Village Council Passes and Annual Periodic Pattas, who were not paid compensation for the land acquired, even though their names were included in the Award No.1 of 2012, 276 Page No.# 9/14 filed reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter to be referred as the "Act of 1894") for awarding them market value of their land.
The reference was entertained as L.A. Case No.30/2014, which was allowed by judgment and award dated 05.02.2015.
By the afore-noted award, those 276 land holders were awarded the land value at the rate of Rs.25 per square feet along with solatium and interest as per the Act of 1894.
They were also granted additional compensation for the market value of the land.

But this was because the reference court had held that no distinction can be made between the owners of land having Land Settlement Certificate and owners of land having Periodic pattas and Village Council Passes.
It is necessary here to state that those persons were also paid 30% solatium on the market value and interest at the rate of 12 % per annum.

Another set of land owners approached the District Collector for redetermination of the amount of compensation payable to them by filing an application under Section 28A of the Act of 1894, which was rejected vide order dated 11.05.2016 by the Deputy Collector.

Against the aforesaid rejection, a writ petition was filed by 63 of the writ petitioners vide WP(C)
No.121/2016.

The High Court remanded the matter back to the District Collector for considering the case of the writ petitioners in accordance with law by following the provisions laid down under Section 28A of the Act of 1894.
Accordingly, the D.C., Kolasib, vide his order dated 28.10.2016 made assessment under Section 28A of the Act of 1894 and directed for payment of compensation.
Page No.# 10/14 This emboldened other writ petitioners also to approach the High Court for payment of interest under Section 28 of the Act of 1894.
In that instance again, the High Court had directed the D.C. to look into the matter, whereafter they were paid interest on the enhanced value of the land under Section 28A of the Act of 1894.

However,
the same appears to have been denied to the respondent Nos.1 to 53, who too has approached this Court and got the matter remanded to the D.C., Kolasib for necessary re-determination, pursuant to which they got an order in their favour.

The appellants herein challenged such assessment and prayed for setting aside such impugned letter of assessment dated 07.12.2022 made by the District Collector, Kolasib and the consequential letter of the District Collector, Kolasib dated 10.05.2023 and sought for a direction not to give effect to the impugned letter of assessment and the consequential letter and further sought a direction from the Union Of India And 4 Ors vs Sh Lalfakawma And 56 Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160625005/
8 Court to adjust the amount which was paid under Section 34 of the Act of 1894 to 41 respondents mentioned in paragraph 11 of the writ petition with the interest payable under Section 28 of the Act of 1894.
Such a prayer was disallowed by the learned Single Judge by holding that the benefit of interest under Sections 34 and 28 of the Act of 1894 are complementary to each other and therefore, there was no reason available on record for quashing of such assessment of the District Collector or for ordering of any such set-off against the interest on compensation already paid under Section 34 of the Act of 1894.
We have examined the judgment and have gone through the facts of this case.
Page No.# 11/14 The position of law is very clear by now.

sentences.text: Under Section 34 of the Act of 1894, interest is required to be paid on the compensation awarded by the Collector.

When the amount of such compensation is not paid or deposited on or before taking possession of the land, the Collector shall be under an obligation to pay the amount awarded with interest thereon at the rate of 9% per annum from the time of so taking possession until it has been so paid or deposited.
The rate would increase to 15% per annum after one year, which is by way of an amendment carried out in the main Act in the year 1984.
Interest under Section 34 applies to the original compensation amount determined by the Collector under Section 11.
Payment of this interest is mandatory and not discretional and it arises from the delay of payment of the awarded amount, whereas interest under Section 28 is the interest on excess compensation.

If a sum which, in the opinion of the Court, the Collector ought to have awarded as compensation, is in excess of the sum which the Collector did award as compensation, the Court may direct that the Collector shall pay interest on such excess at the rate of 9% per annum from the date on which he took possession of the land to the date of payment of such excess amount ordered by the Court.
This Section, therefore, applies only when the reference Court enhances the compensation under Section 18 of the Act of 1894.
There is yet another distinction which is required to be noticed that interest under Section 28 is discretionary and applies only to the excess amount determined by the Court.

Page No.# 12/14 In the present case, the appellants/State is questioning the assessment under Section 28 of the Act of 1894 on the ground that the respondents were not held to be land owners,
and, therefore, the compensation which was paid to them initially was only with respect to the crops and structures.

It was only later that by the order of the Courts, the distinction between the land owners holding the Land Settlement Certificates and the Village Passes and Pattas were blurred and compensation was paid for the first time under Section 34 of the Act of 1894 including interest thereupon.

sentences.text: Some of the land owners, on litigating the issue, were granted further compensation under Section 28 the Act of 1894 which was never questioned by the appellants/State.

In the present case, the assessment had been made by the District Collector in the same vein,
holding the respondents to be entitled to interest under Section 34 and 28 both.

This contention is based on the ground that the provisions contained in Sections 28 and 34 are complementary and supplementary to each other and that when they were only paid for the crops and structures and not paid for the land, which was paid only later with the intervention of the Court, this was definitely an enhancement, attracting the provision contained in Section 28 the Act of 1894 and therefore, their entitlement for interest under Section 34 as also under Section 28 of the Act of 1894.
The argument is sought to be repelled by the appellants on the ground that it would not have had been the intention of the legislature to provide the land holders with double interest from the same date under Sections 34 and 28 of the Act of 1894.
Page No.# 13/14 The provision has been included only to ensure that the value of the land must reach the land holder and he cannot be denied the interest component on it if the Court finds that the award declared by the Collector and paid to them was not commensurate and thought it good to enhance the compensation amount.
Thus the provision has been made under Section 28 for interest in the same terms as in Section 34 on the enhanced amount.

Both the sides have relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Sunder -Vs- Union of India ::
(2001) 7 SCC 211 but the issue raised here does not appear to have been answered in the afore-noted judgment.

To further specify the issue involved in the present case, the point is whether the interference of the Court in declaring that the respondents also are land holders, whose lands have been appropriated by the N.F. Railways, would amount to enhancement of compensation because they were earlier paid only for the crops and structures.

If the compensation granted to them under Section 34 of the Act of 1894 is taken to be a compensation of the value of the land plus other entitlements adding up to the compensation amount, then whether this situation could be termed as an enhancement of compensation directed by the Court, incurring the liability of the State to pay interest under Section 28 of the Act of 1894 as well.

We were about to decide this case when Mr. A.R. Malholtra, learned Advocate for the respondent Nos.1 to 53 submitted that many of the land holders under the same transaction were paid interest under Section 34 and Section 28 as well, which is not sought to be annulled or varied or rescinded by the State.
Therefore, any attempt at divesting Page No.# 14/14 them of the benefits which has accrued to them by virtue of the order of this Court, should not be taken away.
Mr. H. Gupta, learned Central Government Counsel for the appellants submits that he will get back to the issue after taking necessary instructions in this regard.

opennyai_summary.facts:
They were granted compensation for crops but the compensation for land was granted only to two of the land owners who were found to be holding Land Settlement Certificates.
By the afore-noted award, those 276 land holders were awarded the land value at the rate of Rs.25 per square feet along with solatium and interest as per the Act of 1894.
But this was because the reference court had held that no distinction can be made between the owners of land having Land Settlement Certificate and owners of land having Periodic pattas and Village Council Passes.
The appellants herein challenged such assessment and prayed for setting aside such impugned letter of assessment dated 07.12.2022 made by the District Collector, Kolasib and the consequential letter of the District Collector, Kolasib dated 10.05.2023 and sought for a direction not to give effect to the impugned letter of assessment and the consequential letter and further sought a direction from the Union Of India And 4 Ors vs Sh Lalfakawma And 56 Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160625005/
8 Court to adjust the amount which was paid under Section 34 of the Act of 1894 to 41 respondents mentioned in paragraph 11 of the writ petition with the interest payable under Section 28 of the Act of 1894.
Such a prayer was disallowed by the learned Single Judge by holding that the benefit of interest under Sections 34 and 28 of the Act of 1894 are complementary to each other and therefore, there was no reason available on record for quashing of such assessment of the District Collector or for ordering of any such set-off against the interest on compensation already paid under Section 34 of the Act of 1894.
We have examined the judgment and have gone through the facts of this case.
Page No.# 11/14 The position of law is very clear by now.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Under Section 34 of the Act of 1894, interest is required to be paid on the compensation awarded by the Collector.
When the amount of such compensation is not paid or deposited on or before taking possession of the land, the Collector shall be under an obligation to pay the amount awarded with interest thereon at the rate of 9% per annum from the time of so taking possession until it has been so paid or deposited.
The rate would increase to 15% per annum after one year, which is by way of an amendment carried out in the main Act in the year 1984.
Interest under Section 34 applies to the original compensation amount determined by the Collector under Section 11.
Payment of this interest is mandatory and not discretional and it arises from the delay of payment of the awarded amount, whereas interest under Section 28 is the interest on excess compensation.
If a sum which, in the opinion of the Court, the Collector ought to have awarded as compensation, is in excess of the sum which the Collector did award as compensation, the Court may direct that the Collector shall pay interest on such excess at the rate of 9% per annum from the date on which he took possession of the land to the date of payment of such excess amount ordered by the Court.
This Section, therefore, applies only when the reference Court enhances the compensation under Section 18 of the Act of 1894.
In the present case, the assessment had been made by the District Collector in the same vein,
holding the respondents to be entitled to interest under Section 34 and 28 both.
This contention is based on the ground that the provisions contained in Sections 28 and 34 are complementary and supplementary to each other and that when they were only paid for the crops and structures and not paid for the land, which was paid only later with the intervention of the Court, this was definitely an enhancement, attracting the provision contained in Section 28 the Act of 1894 and therefore, their entitlement for interest under Section 34 as also under Section 28 of the Act of 1894.
The argument is sought to be repelled by the appellants on the ground that it would not have had been the intention of the legislature to provide the land holders with double interest from the same date under Sections 34 and 28 of the Act of 1894.
Page No.# 13/14 The provision has been included only to ensure that the value of the land must reach the land holder and he cannot be denied the interest component on it if the Court finds that the award declared by the Collector and paid to them was not commensurate and thought it good to enhance the compensation amount.
Thus the provision has been made under Section 28 for interest in the same terms as in Section 34 on the enhanced amount.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Both the sides have relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Sunder -Vs- Union of India ::
(2001) 7 SCC 211 but the issue raised here does not appear to have been answered in the afore-noted judgment.
Mr. H. Gupta, learned Central Government Counsel for the appellants submits that he will get back to the issue after taking necessary instructions in this regard.
opennyai_summary.issue: To further specify the issue involved in the present case, the point is whether the interference of the Court in declaring that the respondents also are land holders, whose lands have been appropriated by the N.F. Railways, would amount to enhancement of compensation because they were earlier paid only for the crops and structures.
